basic_identification.name: Are.na
basic_identification.originator: Charles Broskoski (co-founder, product), Daniel Pianetti (operations), Damon Zucconi (engineering), Meg Miller (editorial). Original team included Dena Yago and John Michael Boling.
basic_identification.geography: New York City based. Global user community, heavily concentrated among digital art practitioners, designers, researchers, and cultural workers in North America and Europe.

core_ideas.core_claim: A collaborative knowledge-curation platform that enables deep, interconnected research without algorithmic manipulation. Anti-engagement-metric, anti-advertising, subscription-funded. The closest thing to commons knowledge infrastructure for digital art practitioners.
core_ideas.medium_specificity: Digitally native in its curation model: blocks (content units) can exist in multiple channels simultaneously, creating a non-hierarchical web of associations. This many-to-many relational structure is impossible in physical curation. The platform treats content as research material rather than social media posts.
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: Explicitly resistant. Are.na deliberately avoids algorithmic feeds, push notifications, video-centric engagement, ads, and AI integrations. Discovery is user-driven through search and channel following. The platform positions itself as a refuge from attention-economy platforms. A 2024 podcast described it as 'the Good Web.' Monthly recurring revenue of $114K (2025) demonstrates that an anti-attention business model can sustain itself, if modestly.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Strongly intention-native. Are.na serves declared structural needs: collaborative research, knowledge organization, and community-driven curation. It explicitly refuses to capture engagement or optimize for attention. The subscription model aligns incentives -- the platform serves the user, not advertisers.

market_economics.revenue_model: Freemium subscription. Free tier with limited blocks; paid subscription for unlimited blocks and premium features. Monthly recurring revenue: $114,302 as of 2025. Total expenses: $106,522. No advertising. No venture capital (equity crowdfunding in 2018 with 850 investors, ~75% existing members). Deliberately no-VC to maintain mission alignment.
market_economics.market_position: Infrastructure/tool. Not a marketplace. Serves as the knowledge-curation layer that practitioners use alongside other platforms. Complementary to rather than competing with art marketplaces.
market_economics.price_range: N/A -- Are.na is not an art marketplace. Subscription is approximately $5-7/month for premium features.
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: Slow, steady growth. 13 years of deliberate, non-aggressive scaling. Revenue covers expenses with a small margin. Exploring transition to public benefit corporation or cooperative model by 2025. API v3 in development. The trajectory is sustainability-oriented rather than growth-oriented.
market_economics.collector_demographics: N/A for collectors. User demographics: digital artists, designers, researchers, architects, writers, educators, cultural workers. Heavily concentrated in creative industries. Skews toward practitioners who value research depth over social visibility.
market_economics.sustainability: Currently sustainable at small scale. Revenue exceeds expenses. No debt, no VC pressure. The risk is stagnation rather than collapse -- the platform may not grow fast enough to maintain competitive features. Exploring cooperative ownership models for long-term sustainability. The anti-growth stance is both a strength (mission alignment) and a risk (insufficient investment in product development).

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: Web platform (are.na), API (v2, v3 in development), browser extensions for collecting content. Blocks support text, images, links, embedded media, PDFs. Channels as organizational units. Nested channels for hierarchical structures.
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: Explicitly resistant. Are.na deliberately avoids AI integrations to preserve user agency and community harmony. This is a principled stance against the attention-economy dynamics that AI-powered features typically introduce. However, this also means Are.na cannot offer AI-assisted research, semantic search, or automatic connection-finding.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Static curation with social dynamics. Content is manually curated; channels evolve over time through collaborative addition. No real-time, generative, or automated components.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: Are.na contributes vocabulary around knowledge curation and research practice: blocks, channels, connections, collaborative research, anti-algorithmic design. The platform itself has a distinctive minimal aesthetic that signals its anti-spectacle values. It does not define art-critical vocabulary but provides infrastructure for developing and sharing such vocabulary.
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Strongly openness-leaning (channels are public by default, knowledge is shared). Commons-native (subscription-funded, no enclosure of user data for advertising). Infrastructure over spectacle (deliberately anti-flashy). Collective over individual (collaborative channels, shared research).

infrastructure_governance.openness: Hybrid. Channels are public by default (can be made private). API available. No open-source codebase. Content is accessible but the platform infrastructure is proprietary. Exploring cooperative ownership models.
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: Founding-team governed with community orientation. No formal community governance mechanism. The 2018 crowdfunding created ~850 investor-members but no structured governance rights. Exploring cooperative or public benefit corporation transition. The editorial team (Meg Miller) provides curatorial direction.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: Mixed. Users own their content and can export blocks. However, the relational data (which blocks appear in which channels, the connection graph) is not easily portable. No structured export of the knowledge graph. If Are.na disappears, the connections are lost even if individual content persists elsewhere.
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: Limited. API (v2) provides access to channels and blocks. No support for linked data standards, knowledge graph protocols, or structured metadata interoperability. Content can be imported via browser extension but export is limited. Not graph-ready for external systems.
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: Platform-dependent. No decentralized storage, no blockchain preservation. The Annual book provides some physical archival of community output. Content persists as long as Are.na operates. No redundancy or backup mechanism for the knowledge graph.
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: Basic. Channels can be public, private, or collaboration-only. Block-level privacy is limited. No granular consent for how content is connected or recontextualized when blocks appear across multiple channels. No machine-readable consent standards.

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Parallel but connected. Used by practitioners and students across art schools and cultural institutions. The 2015 Guggenheim collaboration (Azone Futures Market) demonstrated institutional recognition. Not a market player but a research companion to traditional art practice.
field_position.what_it_enables: Collaborative visual and textual research across distributed communities. Non-hierarchical knowledge organization. A space for slow, deep thinking about art and culture without algorithmic pressure. Cross-pollination between disciplines through shared channels.
field_position.what_it_lacks: Structured semantic relations between blocks (connections are implicit, not typed). No knowledge graph functionality. No search beyond keyword matching (no semantic or conceptual search). Limited export and interoperability. No formal ontology or taxonomy. The knowledge is socially organized but not machine-readable.
field_position.who_is_excluded: Non-English speakers (platform and community are primarily anglophone). Those who need AI-assisted research tools. Users accustomed to algorithmic discovery (the manual curation model requires more effort). The subscription cost, while low, may exclude some in the Global South. The cultural context is heavily Western art school and design.
field_position.frontier_signal: Established with frontier potential. The platform itself is mature (13 years) but the model it represents -- anti-algorithmic, subscription-funded, commons-oriented -- is increasingly relevant as a counter-model to AI-driven platforms. The cooperative transition would be genuinely frontier for a platform of this type.

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: User-driven: search, channel following, browsing connected channels. Word of mouth. Editorial (Are.na Annual). No algorithmic recommendation. No push notifications. Discovery requires active exploration.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: Very low. Are.na's survival does not depend on platform attention metrics. It would survive if Twitter/Instagram disappeared -- its user base finds it through institutional recommendations, word of mouth, and direct search. The subscription model insulates it from attention-economy fluctuations.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: Strongly intention-native. The platform exists to serve knowledge curation and collaborative research. No engagement optimization, no advertising, no data extraction. The subscription model ensures the user is the customer, not the product.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: Significant in practice, limited in structure. Are.na hosts enormous amounts of shared knowledge (public channels on art, design, culture). But this knowledge is not structured, not machine-readable, and not exportable as a knowledge graph. The commons contribution is social rather than infrastructural -- it exists within Are.na's walls rather than as open data.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Neither ownership nor meaning formally. Blocks have timestamps and attribution. Channel curation history is visible. But there is no provenance tracking in the art-world sense.
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Archival (content persists) with social temporality (channels evolve over time through community additions). The Annual publication introduces a cyclical editorial temporality.
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: Does not explicitly address absence. However, the open channel model allows communities to surface gaps -- users can create channels around what is missing, underrepresented, or overlooked. This is emergent rather than designed.

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Coherence by design. Multiple channels can contain the same block with different contextualizations. No single authority on how content should be classified. The platform enables diverse readings to coexist without forcing consensus.
coherence.contestability: Informal. Users can create alternative channels that reframe content differently. There is no formal contestation mechanism, but the open channel structure allows dissenting perspectives to exist alongside dominant ones. Community norms are soft rather than codified.
coherence.forkability: Low forkability at the platform level (proprietary code). High forkability at the content level -- any user can create a new channel that reframes or recontextualizes existing blocks. However, forking the entire platform would require rebuilding the social graph and community, which is the primary value.

adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: The anti-algorithmic, subscription-funded model as proof that intention-native platforms can survive financially. The many-to-many block-to-channel model (content existing in multiple contexts simultaneously) as a pattern for relational knowledge. The collaborative research ethos. The Annual publication as a model for periodic synthesis. The cooperative ownership exploration.
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: The lack of structured semantic relations. Are.na's connections are implicit and social, not typed or machine-readable. A(DAI) needs the relational depth that Are.na lacks: typed edges, ontological structure, graph-readiness. Also refuse the closed codebase and limited interoperability. Are.na proves the social model works but does not solve the infrastructure problem.
adai_comparison.structural_tension: Are.na demonstrates that anti-algorithmic knowledge curation has a viable community and business model. A(DAI) wants the same ethos but with structured graph infrastructure underneath. The tension is between Are.na's social looseness (which enables serendipity and creative freedom) and A(DAI)'s need for structured relations (which enable machine reasoning and cross-system interoperability). Can you add structure without killing the organic quality?

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: Minimal. Standard web platform regulations. GDPR compliance for European users. No AI Act exposure (no AI features). No crypto/blockchain regulatory exposure. Privacy-first design reduces regulatory surface area.
regulatory_legal.ip_model: User-owned content. Are.na does not claim IP over user-contributed blocks. Content licensing depends on what users share (links, images, text). No platform-level license assertion beyond terms of service.
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Opt-in. Users choose to create accounts, contribute blocks, and join channels. Public channels are visible to all but participation requires account creation. No opt-out needed because there is no algorithmic tracking or data extraction to opt out of.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: Self-hosted web platform with standard cloud infrastructure. No blockchain dependency. No marketplace dependency. The primary dependency is on the community itself -- if the community migrates, the platform's value collapses.
ecosystem.network_effects: Moderate positive network effects. More users create more channels, making the platform more valuable for research. However, the anti-growth stance limits the scale of these effects. The network is deep (highly engaged users) rather than broad (mass adoption).
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: Not directly affected by NFT crash as Are.na is not a crypto/NFT platform. Steady growth throughout 2022-2025. The crash may have benefited Are.na by driving practitioners away from speculative platforms toward research-oriented ones. Revenue growing modestly; expenses covered. The platform's position strengthens as attention-economy fatigue grows.
